Subject: PromptPilot / TraceLens: connector onboarding — safety & telemetry

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. PromptPilot is ready to move forward with an official connector to Redwood so our customers can route model calls via TraceLens runtime. Before we start engineering work we need a short safety and telemetry gating checklist from your side so we can align on what data is collected, sampling rates, and what attestation we need to provide for our security team.

High-level asks:
- A short list of required telemetry fields (tokens, latency, model id, error codes) and any PII redaction expectations.
- Sampling/retention guidance and whether Redwood exposes a telemetry webhook or S3 export.
- Any onboarding attestation language we need to sign for compliance (SOC/PII).

Attached is our connector spec draft (pp_connector_questions.pdf) and a one-pager on TraceLens runtime. Could you loop in the right owners at Redwood who can sign off? Wed like to have a gating checklist by next week.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, PromptPilot

Subject: RE: PromptPilot / TraceLens: connector onboarding — safety & telemetry

Thanks — I started a draft of the telemetry-field-matrix and attached it. High-level notes below; see attachment for CSV with field types and retention recommendations.

Telemetry matrix (summary):
- Required (for all connector calls): timestamp_utc, request_id, model_id, token_count_request, token_count_response, latency_ms, status_code, error_subcode
- Optional (instrumentation / quality): prompt_bucket, prompt_template_id, user_tier, sampling_label
- PII: we do NOT store user message bodies by default. Any text captured must be explicitly redacted before storage. If PromptPilot requires text-level traces for debugging we require a signed attestation and a temporary, short retention window (30d) with audit logging.
- Sampling: default 0.5% full payload capture for large customers; 5% for early-stage pilots. We can raise sampling for debugging by request but need an audit entry.
- Exports / webhooks: Redwood can export aggregated telemetry to an S3 bucket (preferred) or a streaming webhook (signed requests). S3 export supports encrypted-at-rest output and lifecycle rules.

Attached: telemetry-field-matrix.csv (columns: field, type, required, retention_days, redaction_required). Also attaching a short spec pp_connector_spec_v1.xlsx with mapping notes.

Open questions for PromptPilot:
1) For pilot customers, do you need request/response payloads for debugging, or will aggregated metrics suffice?
2) Do your legal requirements mandate a different retention window than 30 days?

Hi Samira / Devendra,

Thanks for your patience — confirming Redwood is good to proceed with the connector pilot under the following gating items. Once these are acknowledged well schedule the technical kickoff.

Gating checklist (agreed):
- Telemetry matrix accepted (required fields as per telemetry-field-matrix.csv).
- Text-level payload capture only by exception: PromptPilot to submit attestation and justification; retention capped at 30 days.
- S3 export configured for your sandbox account (we will provide bucket name and IAM role).
- Sampling defaults applied (0.5% production, 5% pilot); adjustable during controlled debug windows.
- Onboarding attestation: weve attached a short PDF (onboarding-checklist.pdf) with the language our security team requires — please review and confirm any redlines to marissa.cole@redwood.ai.

Timeline:
- Confirm attachments and attestation by EOD Friday 7/9.
- Redwood provides sandbox S3 credentials the week of 7/12 and a 60-minute technical kickoff (we propose 7/14).

Logistics: hubspot deal HS-2390 will be updated with acceptance and well track milestone completion there: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/2390

Please reply with a single-line ACK (accept checklist) or list redlines so we can move to kickoff planning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
